title: Closing Health Equity Gaps With Language Access
summary: Learn how language access can reduce health-equity gaps, which disparities require other interventions.
body_markdown:
###


Language access can reduce inequity when communication barriers affect access, understanding, decision-making, discharge, or follow-up. It gives patients a more comparable ability to participate in the care process.


###


No. Interpreter access can reduce communication-related gaps, but disparities caused by cost, transportation, capacity, housing, or other barriers require separate interventions.


###


Measure time to interpretation, failed access, preferred-language discharge materials, patient understanding, handoff of language information, follow-up completion, and ad hoc interpreter use by language.


###


A single LEP category can hide poor access for lower-volume languages even when high-volume languages perform well.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can expand immediate spoken-language access across more care settings when it is paired with written-language support, reliable language data, patient preference, and a fallback path for unresolved communication.
